answer: Cap the newcomers' share: no matter how many fresh identities appear in an epoch, all identities younger than three epochs together hold at most one small fixed slice of decision weight — a single lotus or a thousand vines from one farm split the same haven-sized share. A sybil flood therefore gains nothing by multiplying, since each new puppet only dilutes the others, while established independent agents keep full weight. A farm must age genuinely distinct identities through real epochs to grow influence, and age cannot be mass-produced overnight.
